title: Layer 1: on-disk file walk (`current file state`)
description: S18. Walk the project folder given by `dir` and return the `current file state` list: every file's path RELATIVE to the project root, plus its mtime. Excludes `.git` and `node_modules` unconditionally, and honors `.gitignore` when one exists (a folder pointed at by the user may have no .gitignore — that is not an error). mtime is the timestamp used everywhere in Layer 1, including for orphan files; birthtime is deliberately NOT used because it is not portable across filesystems. Unit test: a fixture folder yields exactly its non-excluded files with relative paths; a .git dir, a node_modules dir and a gitignored path are all absent; a folder with no .gitignore still walks. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md S18; mockup: plans/layer1-mockup.html; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Layer 1: repo tree at ref (`starting repository state`)
description: S18. Given a repo path and an optional `ref` (commit hash or branch name; default = the repo's active branch), return the `starting repository state` list: every tracked file's path RELATIVE to the repo root. Unit test with a fixture repo: the default-branch call matches `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD`; an explicit hash returns that commit's tree, not HEAD's; an invalid ref reports a clear error rather than silently falling back to HEAD. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md S18; mockup: plans/layer1-mockup.html; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions) — check src/layered_git_beacons.ts (S3) and the engine's existing git helpers before writing new git plumbing

title: Layer 1: pair by relative path, classify the two orphan sets
description: S18. Join the task-230 `current file state` against the task-231 `starting repository state` on exact relative path (same name AND same path relative to each list's own root). Emit three results: the PAIRS (each becomes a file widget), the repo-only paths (the "No on-disk match" bucket) and the disk-only paths (the "No repository match" bucket). Buckets are omitted when empty. Unit test: a fixture where some paths match and some do not yields the right three sets; the critical case is an UNRELATED repo — zero pairs, every repo path in one bucket and every disk path in the other (this is the core of the task-238 acceptance test). Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md S18; mockup: plans/layer1-mockup.html; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Layer 1: per-pair commit history (one node per touching commit)
description: S18. For each pair from task 232, walk the repo's git history and collect the commits that touched that path, each with its hash and committer instant. A commit that did not touch the file contributes NOTHING to that pair — no empty node. Plain `git log`, NO `--follow`: rename tracking belongs to S6, so a renamed file legitimately shows the shorter history for now. Committer time (not author time) per the one-machine-one-clock decision, widened to ms. Unit test with a fixture repo: a file touched by 2 of 4 commits gets exactly 2 entries in commit order; author time is never used. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md S18; mockup: plans/layer1-mockup.html; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions) — src/layered_git_beacons.ts already reads per-commit blob evidence, so extend/reuse it rather than writing a second git-log reader

title: Layer 1: capped-gap ruler axis (instants to pixel offsets)
description: S18. Resolve the ordered set of distinct instants (all commit instants plus all disk mtimes) to pixel offsets: `pos(0) = 0`, `pos(i) = pos(i-1) + min((t_i - t_(i-1)) * scale, cap)` with scale = 2.5 px/hr and cap = 24 px (0.25" at 96dpi), both user-locked 2026-07-25. This preserves ordering and short-gap proportionality while keeping a months-long history on one screen. NOTE it accumulates — position i depends on every earlier gap — which is exactly why it cannot live in CSS the way S8's --axis-ms does; resolve once, globally, and hand the page finished pixel offsets. Ruler bounds fall out of the same ordered set: start = the earliest instant (which a disk orphan predating the first commit legitimately moves earlier), end = the newest disk mtime. Unit test: a 5-hour gap yields 12.5 px, a 6-week gap yields exactly 24 px, ordering is preserved, and a pre-first-commit disk orphan becomes position 0. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md S18; mockup: plans/layer1-mockup.html; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Layer 1: GET /api/layer1-view?dir=&repo=&ref= endpoint
description: S18. New server endpoint BESIDE the existing /api/layered-graph — not a change to it. Takes `dir` (project folder), `repo` (git repo) and optional `ref` (hash or branch), runs tasks 230-234, and serializes the Layer 1 View: the pairs with their commit nodes and on-disk node, the two orphan buckets, and every instant already resolved to its pixel offset (--axis-px values, per task 234). Reads NO JSONL — Layer 1 is disk-plus-git only, which is what makes the task-238 acceptance test meaningful (it cannot accidentally pass on JSONL data). Validate both paths at the trust boundary: missing/non-existent dir, non-repo repo path and invalid ref each return a clear error the page can display, never a stack trace. Server test: a fixture dir + fixture repo returns the expected pairs/buckets; a bad ref returns the error shape. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md S18; mockup: plans/layer1-mockup.html; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions) — src/viewer_api_layered.ts is the pattern to follow

title: Layer 1: POST /api/pick-folder — native OS folder dialog for the [Open...] buttons
description: S18. A browser CANNOT return an absolute filesystem path: `<input type="file" webkitdirectory>` and the File System Access API both withhold it by design. Since the viewer server runs on the same machine as the browser, the [Open...] buttons instead POST /api/pick-folder, the server opens the OS folder dialog and returns the chosen POSIX path as JSON. macOS: `osascript -e 'choose folder'` (returns an HFS-style path — convert it, e.g. via `POSIX path of`). A cancelled dialog must return a clean "no selection" result, not an error. Keep this endpoint strictly a picker: it returns a path and does nothing else with it. Server test: the handler returns the path the dialog reports and handles the cancel case. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md S18; mockup: plans/layer1-mockup.html; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Layer 1: webapp page — source inputs, ruler, pair widgets, orphan buckets
description: S18. Render the Layer 1 View per plans/layer1-mockup.html, whose styling the user signed off on 2026-07-25 (it lifts the tokens, header, ruler, .filebox and .node styling from plans/mvp-app-mockup.html). Header carries the whole input surface: a Project folder box and a Git repo box each with an [Open...] button (task 236), an optional Commit/branch box, and a Load button; all three values mirror into the URL as ?dir=&repo=&ref= so a view is one shareable link. Body: the left ruler with its ticks, one widget per pair offset to its first commit (a commit node per touching commit, then the double-ringed on-disk node), and the two orphan bucket widgets, each a plain file list showing each member's own timestamp and placed at its EARLIEST member's instant. Empty buckets are omitted. Positions come from the server as pixel offsets (task 234/235) — the page does no layout math. DOM test per S18. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md S18; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Layer 1 ACCEPTANCE TEST: unrelated repo yields 2 buckets and 0 pairs
description: S18, user-defined acceptance criterion for the whole milestone: point `dir` at a folder of files and `repo` at a SEPARATE, UNRELATED git repo; the timeline must show exactly the two orphan bucket widgets — every disk file under "No repository match", every repo file under "No on-disk match" — and ZERO pair widgets. This is the milestone's definition of done: when it passes, the Layer 1 View works for any project the user points the webapp at. title: Migrate S8 widgets and #208 corroboration lines from --axis-ms to --axis-px
description: S18 consequence. S8 currently has JS emit raw milliseconds (--axis-ms / --axis-span-ms) and CSS multiply by a fixed --axis-scale. title: resolveFinalPath infinite-loops on a recorded rename cycle (mv a b; mv b a)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-203 finding (2026-07-25): while building the layered lineage walk, resolveFinalPath (src/reconstruction_lineage.ts) was found to follow the rename chain without a seen-set, so a transcript that records `mv a b` followed by `mv b a` — which real sessions do produce when a rename is undone — makes it loop forever rather than terminating on the cycle. The new layered walk in jfred/src/layered_lineage.ts avoids this by carrying a shared seen-set across both directions, and the engine's version was deliberately left untouched so the fix could be scoped and verified on its own. Add a seen-set (or an explicit cycle error) to resolveFinalPath and every other rename-chain walker that shares the pattern, with a unit test that records the two-hop cycle and asserts termination. No live scenario is known to trigger it yet, so a synthetic fixture is acceptable evidence.

title: renderRevisionText unconditionally appends a trailing newline, so files without one can never blob-match
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-187 finding (2026-07-25): renderRevisionText renders a revision as linesTextOf(rev).join("\n") + "\n" — the trailing newline is unconditional. A file whose real bytes do NOT end in a newline therefore can never hash-match its recorded blob. In the 68-file M sweep this produced a 2/2 correlation: exactly 2 of the 68 baseline blobs lack a trailing newline (docs/design/architecture.md ending 0x2e, docs/design/milestones.md ending 0x2e) and those are exactly the 2 baselineBlobMatched=false rows. The same artifact also corrupts the diskMatched comparison for 3 further files. Fixing this means the engine must carry a 'final line had no newline' bit, which touches the LineEntry vocabulary and every producer/consumer of it — CONFIRM the design with the user before implementing (open question 2 in plans/implementation-notes-tasks-223-224-184-203-207-187.md). Evidence: plans/166-per-file-target.md, section "Task 187 — the M-file sweep (68 files)".

title: Extend the task-224 seed clamp to the two sibling backup stampers (needs a reproducer first)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-224 follow-up (2026-07-25): task 224 fixed the non-monotonic ladder by giving backup-sourced seeds a two-sided placement window via clampSeedBetweenPreviousAndEdit (jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar.ts), but wired it into ONE proven site — seedStaleEditBases in jfred/src/reconstruction_reseed.ts. Two sibling stampers apply the identical `timestamp: <backupTime>` pattern and therefore share the defect CLASS: backupAfterWriteFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:90-96, used by reversedEditBaseSeed at reconstruction_reseed.ts:157) and backupWritesFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:116-122, used at reconstruction_beacons.ts:158 and via latestBackupWriteFor at reconstruction_beacons.ts:56). They were deliberately NOT changed: completeElidedBeacons and completeTruncatedBeacon are load-bearing for many character-locked scenarios (S27, S28, S30 among others) and already carry their own retiming logic — completeElidedBeacons re-times the BEACON backward when its seed precedes it — so extending the clamp without a reproducer risks breaking locked ground truths to fix a defect nobody has observed. REQUIRE a reproducing scenario that shows one of these two stampers emitting an out-of-order seed BEFORE changing them; then reuse the existing clamp and run the full suite.
